notes: `נַפְשִׁי` → *me* fuses noun and suffix into the one English pronoun that carries both senses (rule 30), with the competing reading marking `נֶפֶשׁ` `unrepresented` named in the unit's note.

*all his* before `כֹּחַ` answers to no morpheme — no `כֹּל` and no suffix stands in the phrase — and the two supplied words stand together doing one office, so they are a single `added` unit (rules 18, 30, 2).
`בּוֹ` → *therein* carries the clause's copula in its own unit (rules 22, 49), and the comparative `מִן` takes the bare *than* (rule 24).
